extracted.intended_audience: Department of the Navy commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), and DON personnel responsible for public information and media relations
extracted.subtask_description: Official Department of the Navy public affairs instruction describing roles, responsibilities, standards, release authorities, media-embedding procedures, community relations, and constraints for PAOs and commanders when producing and releasing public information (including press releases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with other military and civilian PAOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Will communicate with other military and civilian PAOs as helpful or appropriate for coordination or mutual assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform chain about items with broad media or security interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Will inform the immediate public affairs chain of command about items with national or international media interest; those with local media interest when expected to reach the attention of flag or general officers; and those involving real, perceived or anticipated security breeches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote positive relations with local communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Will promote positive relations between the command and local communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol function separation
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol function is not necessarily included in the public affairs mission. These functions should be separate unless extraordinary circumstances dictate otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-duty PAO private-publication constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs acting in a private capacity may prepare information for public release through non-DOD forums or media only if specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (a) No laws or regulations are violated; (b) Ethical standards and compliance are maintained (See DODD 5500.7); (c) Preparation activities are not conducted during normal duty hours or using DOD facilities, property, or personnel except as authorized; (d) No official DON information is released which is not generally available to the public (See DODD 5400.7-R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate information release with subject-matter experts and offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Information release will be coordinated with the appropriate offices, subject-matter experts, and/or activities both internal and external to the command. PAOs should consult or create applicable public affairs guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 2 and Chapter 3 supplemental guidance for detailed procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release at lowest appropriate command level
rubrics_metrics.description: Information will be released at the lowest appropriate level of command unless other guidance dictates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands will evaluate factors such as subject matter, anticipated impact, scope of expected media coverage (local or national), and in the case of speeches, prominence of the speaking venue; determine if coordination with other commands, offices, or government agencies is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize news media and public inquiries; support from other DON offices
rubrics_metrics.description: News media and public inquiries will be treated as a priority. Other DON offices and activities can be directed by CHINFO to support PAOs in preparing appropriate information release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate for accuracy and consistent messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: All PAOs with some responsibility on an issue will closely collaborate to ensure accuracy and comprehensiveness, and that all spokespersons have the same information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 3 for additional guidance on spokesperson procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding information — not arbitrary; release facts and avoid speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Information cannot be withheld arbitrarily or merely to avoid criticism or embarrassment. Release fact and decline to speculate or offer an opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "No comment" is never an appropriate response. Acceptable alternatives include: (a) "I have nothing to release on that subject." (used when absolutely no response is appropriate), and (b) "An investigation is under way, and it would be inappropriate for me to comment at this time." (for matters under formal investigation). See Chapter 1, 0101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death reporting and next-of-kin notification
rubrics_metrics.description: When a DON member dies, the local command may not be the releasing authority of the information and must adhere to next-of-kin notification guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 2 and Chapter 8 for specific next-of-kin and casualty release procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely dissemination for events of intense public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: For mishaps, accidents, emergencies, and similar high-interest events, information will be disseminated fully, candidly and promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First release of what happened should be made within one hour of command awareness of an event. Failure or tardiness may be interpreted as concealment. See Chapter 8 for supplemental guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with topics requiring higher-level release authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain topics are subject to more intense review and higher level of release; commanders and PAOs must be familiar with these areas and seek advice from the chain of command when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 2 for specifics on topics requiring elevated review and release authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website content approval and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands must create and maintain a clear process for establishing, reviewing, and ensuring ongoing maintenance and accuracy of public Web sites. The command’s release authority (usually the Commander or the PAO) must approve items posted on a public website or any site with open access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 12 for detailed web and digital media guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive media relations posture
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders will support a proactive media relations posture to help build and maintain key relationships with members of the mass media; delaying responses undermines relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate media support in all command plans, including operational plans, to ensure internal and external audiences receive necessary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination and approval for national/international media releases
rubrics_metrics.description: All information provided to national or international news media must be coordinated with the chain of command and approved in advance by CHINFO or DIRPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a command learns a news report will receive wide attention, inform CHINFO or DIRPA via chain of command and include a description of circumstances and proposed responses (or actions already taken) — for fast-breaking news provide what was already done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertainment/media production support approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for Navy or Marine Corps support for national or international productions will be forwarded with details and recommendations to CHINFO or DIRPA for ASD(PA) approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a commercial film produced with DON cooperation is screened locally, nearby commands may provide exhibits, recruiting material displays, and arrange personal appearances only if approved by CHINFO, DIRPA, and ASD(PA). Approval is not required when DON personnel attend as audience members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for DON personnel participation in media programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Appearance of Navy or Marine Corps members in programs is authorized when certain criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation authorized only if: (1) No endorsement of commercial products or services is given or implied; (2) Participation is dignified and in keeping with standards; (3) Compatible with operational commitments; (4) Does not place members in competition with professional performers seeking employment; (5) Individual desires to participate; (6) The individual is in an unofficial and off-duty status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial advertising and promotional activity approval and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests from commercial enterprises to use DON members, equipment, or facilities for advertising must be approved by CHINFO or DIRPA and must conform to standards of conduct and Joint Ethics Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision is based primarily on whether an endorsement is made or implied and whether such support could bring discredit to the Navy or Marine Corps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media embark general guidelines (services provided and transport)
rubrics_metrics.description: When embarking News Media Representatives (NMRs) in DON ships and aircraft, certain logistical and conduct guidelines apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military transportation shall not compete with commercial sources (exceptions: orientation flights or in DON's best interests); basic services like messing provided on reimbursable basis; NMRs normally granted privileges of an O-4 or above for messing and transportation and billeting when convenient; journalists may use enlisted berthing in some situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval authority for media embarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Fleet Commanders or applicable Combatant Commander have approval authority for all media embarks except national/international media which require CHINFO or ASD(PA) approval. Delegation allowed to three-star subordinates or Navy Component Commanders as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA representation and media embark planning requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All operations shall include plans to embark NMRs and public affairs representation is essential in operation planning to meet commander’s responsibilities to news media coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 3 and Chapter 6 for planning and execution details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media access during operations
rubrics_metrics.description: NMRs will be given access to U.S. military operations from the first stages through completion and subsequent post-operation activity; access may include embedding with specific units and embarks aboard ships and aircraft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation guidance for NMRs (local vs non-local travel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for approving local travel and non-local travel for NMRs, including justification requirements and coordination obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local travel may be approved by commanders if: (1) subject matter not responsibility of higher command; (2) public interest limited to the mission/vicinity; (3) travel supports local PA program meeting a DON PA objective; (4) supports NMR arrival/departure (short trips). Non-local travel: submit requests to CHINFO or DIRPA to forward with recommendations to CNO or CMC and, if necessary, ASD(PA); coordinate with Combatant Command if within their AOR; foreign travel requires embassy and theater clearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embarkation on MSC and Maritime Prepositioning Ships
rubrics_metrics.description: NMRs may be embarked on Military Sealift Command vessels when in DON or DOD best interests; requests to embark on Maritime Prepositioning Ships must be forwarded to CHINFO via DIRPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with MSC PA for MSC vessel embarks; may be space-required or space-available.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASD(PA) approval for reimbursable travel on DOD aircraft
rubrics_metrics.description: ASD(PA) is responsible for approving travel or transportation by DOD-owned or -controlled aircraft used for PA programs, including reimbursable travel arranged jointly with other federal departments, agencies, or foreign governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of Public Affairs (PA) and Information Operations (IO)
rubrics_metrics.description: PA and IO activities must remain separate because their principal audiences and intents differ; PA focuses on informing public and international audiences while IO influences adversary audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA will not disseminate false information, use PA products as military deception, or provide disinformation. While coordination/synchronization with IO is required, PA should maintain institutional credibility by remaining separate from PSYOP/IO functions; PA personnel should work directly for the commander and not be subordinate to IO.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA will not perform PSYOP or allow PSYOP to address media
rubrics_metrics.description: PA activity is separate from IO/PSYOP; PA will never engage in PSYOP activities and PSYOP personnel will not address national or international media unless specifically related to PSYOP coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate facilities must be made available for PA and PSYOP activities; PA will not be primary spokesperson when working with IO cell.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA contribution to countering misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: PA may contribute to information strategies developed to counter misinformation and propaganda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination and synchronization among all parties (PA, IO, CA) required to ensure messages and themes are de-conflicted and do not contradict each other, preserving credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA roles in military operations (planning and readiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs will support the commander's responsibility during operations by sharing guidance, ensuring commander awareness of requirements, participating in planning and exercises, planning/executing CPICs/JIBs, and providing on-site media training or ad-hoc guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public affairs planning must be included in every phase of the operational plan and developed in close coordination with the overall operational plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications support for media in absence of commercial facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of commercial communications difficulties, NMRs are authorized to file stories via expeditious military signal/communications capabilities, but should use commercial communications whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Military communications support shall not come at the expense of critical military communications; communication restrictions (to protect unit locations) must be used only when necessary and included in media ground rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistical support obligations to embedded media
rubrics_metrics.description: Units should plan lift and logistical support to move media products to/from the battlefield and support NMRs while in the AOR, including billeting, messing, communications and transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transportation assets dedicated to support maximum coverage will be provided on a space-available, no-additional-cost-to-government basis; provide space for necessary media equipment when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community relations objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: COMREL programs shall support objectives: create and sustain partnerships with publics at home and abroad; support equal opportunity and non-discrimination policy; increase public awareness and understanding of Navy and Marine Corps; support recruiting goals; inspire patriotism through observance of traditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must maintain adequate files and continuity records on COMREL programs; instruction cancels previously required reports to CHINFO but records may be crucial for future queries and events.

rubrics_metrics.name: COMREL participation fundamentals
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders overseeing COMREL programs must ensure support is appropriate, does not selectively benefit any entity, reflects positively on the Naval services, and complies with DOD/DON policies, Joint Ethics Regulations and safety standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See supplemental guidance for detailed COMREL participation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propriety standards for community relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands shall avoid support that might create the appearance of using a Government position for private gain, selectively benefit any person/organization, impair Government efficiency or economy, lose independence or impartiality, circumvent official channels, or cause loss of public confidence in Government integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval levels for COMREL programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for COMREL programs exceeding a commander's purview, local capability, or policy scope will be referred up the chain of command using DD Form 2536; CHINFO, DIRPA and/or ASD(PA) are approval authority for specified national/regional programs and other listed categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples requiring CHINFO/DIRPA/ASD(PA) approval include: NCR support (except non-foreign speaking engagements), national/international programs/conventions, liaison with national NGOs, information/support to national organizations, aerial reviews involving more than one service, sporting events of national scope, programs requiring liaison with DOD/Washington offices, appearance on regional/national broadcast by performance units, and programs requiring exceptions to DOD policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-border and overseas event coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders may participate in local events jointly planned with US-Mexico-Canada border communities with full coordination with State Department officials; Combatant Commanders approve overseas public events and implement COMREL programs within their AOR but may delegate authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DON components receive COMREL guidance from the combatant commander or joint task force commander when delegated; programs impacting a combatant command must coordinate through appropriate channels when support will impact operations, require major support, or draw media/host nation interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising restrictions and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: All DOD components must conform to government-wide charitable fundraising policy administered by OPM; charitable and fundraising support beyond the CFC is restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD members shall not officially endorse or appear to endorse any non-Federal entity, event, product, service, or enterprise; events may not selectively benefit any group; fundraising events for a single cause are inconsistent with DOD policy; general internal publicity for CFC or service-specific campaigns is allowed but PAOs/editors must not appear to favor single charities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted membership drives and fundraising exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership drives and fundraising for specified entities are allowed under conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed: (1) Combined Federal Campaign; (2) Emergency and disaster appeals approved by OPM; (3) Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society and other approved service-specific charities; (4) Private organizations composed primarily of DOD members raising funds among members for welfare funds for their own members (requires approval by the head [of command]).
